source_name: Agencija za mirno rješavanje radnih sporova (AMRRS) – Montenegro Agency for Peaceful Resolution of Labour Disputes
why_relevant: Statutory body handling individual and collective labour disputes free of charge; mediators handle collective disputes (incl. strike-related) and arbitrators decide individual dismissal cases. Filings naming a bank as employer are legally generated, adversarial evidence of restructuring or forced exits that management will not announce.

source_name: Zakon o mirnom rješavanju radnih sporova (PDF, hosted by Unija poslodavaca CG)
why_relevant: Defines what a collective vs individual labour dispute is, who must file and what is recorded — the legal grammar needed to interpret AMRRS outputs and to know which restructuring events generate a mandatory paper trail.

source_name: Unija slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore (USSCG) – Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro
why_relevant: One of the two national confederations; explicitly founded in 2007 by an initiative that included bank sector trade unions ('sindikati ... banaka'). Confederation statements, protest calls and wage/redundancy disputes surface bank workforce actions before employers comment.

source_name: Savez sindikata Crne Gore (SSCG) – Confederation of Trade Unions of Montenegro
why_relevant: The older national confederation and the counterpart signatory to sectoral collective agreements; its branch unions cover financial organisations. Its statements and collective-bargaining positions expose redundancy plans and disputes in banks.

source_name: Granski kolektivni ugovor za banke, druge finansijske organizacije i osiguranje u Crnoj Gori (sector collective agreement)
why_relevant: The banking-sector branch collective agreement, signed between the financial-organisations union and Unija poslodavaca. It sets redundancy severance floors (e.g. up to 36 net salaries for long-service staff declared tehnološki višak) and consultation duties — i.e. it defines the cost and the procedure any bank restructuring must follow, and identifies the union counterparty by name.

source_name: Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore (UPCG) – collective agreements library
why_relevant: Employer-side signatory of the banking branch agreement; its library aggregates branch collective agreements and labour-law texts, and its statements reveal the employer position on redundancies and collective-agreement extension. Also a pointer to which employer bodies represent banks.

source_name: Uprava za inspekcijske poslove Crne Gore – Odsjek za inspekciju rada (Labour Inspectorate) annual work reports
why_relevant: Labour inspectorate supervises employment relations, dismissals and workplace safety; its izvještaj o radu documents inspections, complaints and sanctions and can be filtered by activity sector. Worker complaints against banks appear here before they reach the press.

source_name: Sudovi Crne Gore – judicial portal, court decisions (odluke) search
why_relevant: Anonymised judgments of basic, higher, commercial and Supreme courts. Labour-dispute judgments (radni spor, poništaj odluke o otkazu) naming banks as defendants are the hardest evidence of forced exits of staff and of managers, and of the timing of restructuring waves.

source_name: Portal pravosuđa Crne Gore (pravosudje.me)
why_relevant: Umbrella judiciary portal pointing to individual courts, case-tracking services and judicial statistics — the navigation layer for finding which court hears labour disputes against banks in a given municipality.

source_name: PROPISINET.ME – Sudska praksa sudova Crne Gore (commercial case-law database)
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of Montenegrin case law with advanced search, export and an email alert service for newly entered decisions in a chosen legal area — a practical monitoring layer for labour-law judgments involving banks.

source_name: Socijalni savjet Crne Gore (Social Council – tripartite body)
why_relevant: Tripartite forum (government, unions, employers) where general and branch collective agreements, wage coefficients and redundancy policy are contested. Session agendas and minutes reveal union escalation and employer plans affecting the finance sector.

source_name: CdM – Cafe del Montenegro (economy section)
why_relevant: Covers Social Council sessions, collective-agreement negotiations and employer statements — the tripartite layer where sector-wide redundancy and pay terms for banks are decided.

source_name: Kodex.me – labour/collective agreement reporting
why_relevant: Covers the state of the general collective agreement and worker rights disputes; a secondary outlet that sometimes carries union positions the mainstream skips.

source_name: Zaštitnik ljudskih prava i sloboda Crne Gore (Ombudsman) – annual and special reports
why_relevant: Handles discrimination and mobbing complaints, including workplace cases, and must publish annual reports with statistics by area. Mobbing/discrimination complaints are a recognised proxy for pressure on staff during restructuring or forced management exits.

source_name: ETUI trade union profiles – Montenegro (USSCG and SSCG entries)
why_relevant: European Trade Union Institute directory profiling Montenegrin confederations, their affiliation and branch structure — the fastest route to the correct legal names of the finance/banking branch unions and their European affiliations (UNI Europa Finance).

source_name: UNI Europa Finance
why_relevant: European federation of ~100 finance-sector unions; publishes statements on bank restructuring, branch closures and digitalisation-driven job cuts, and can identify the Montenegrin bank union as an affiliate. Cross-border group restructurings (NLB, OTP, Erste, Addiko) often surface here before local disclosure.

source_name: ILO EPLex / NATLEX – Montenegro collective dismissal procedures and labour inspection texts
why_relevant: Standardised description of Montenegro's collective-dismissal thresholds and duties (20+ employees in 90 days triggers the procedure; consultation with the union and notification of the employment bureau; 15-day pre-decision consultation on restructuring; 6-month re-hiring ban). This is the rulebook that tells the analyst which bank restructurings must produce a public trace.

source_name: Law-firm labour-law briefings on Montenegro (Karanović & Partners, BDK Advokati, Schoenherr, Mondaq)
why_relevant: Practitioner commentary on the Labour Act sets out redundancy thresholds, severance floors, consultation duties and the 6-month re-hiring ban — the interpretive layer needed to read bank restructuring announcements and to anticipate cost. Firms also flag amendments in advance of employer behaviour changes.

source_name: Decent Work Balkans – Montenegro Fact Sheet
why_relevant: Regional labour-rights monitoring project publishing country fact sheets on union density, collective bargaining coverage and dispute practice — context for judging how much of a bank's workforce is unionised and therefore how visible a restructuring will be.

source_name: Mojazarada.me – Zakon o radu / sindikat explainer
why_relevant: Montenegrin worker-facing explainer of union rights, representativeness thresholds and strike rules in local language — useful for the cell glossary and for judging when a bank union becomes a legally recognised bargaining counterparty.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL) Balkan service – Montenegro labour-law coverage
why_relevant: Independent regional outlet with substantive coverage of Montenegrin labour-law change (e.g. abolition of 'blanko otkazi') and of mass dismissals of managers in state-linked institutions — a model for detecting politically driven leadership purges that also touch state-owned financial institutions.

source_name: MINA news agency (mina.news) – business/labour wire
why_relevant: National news agency carrying institutional labour stories including AMRRS workload expectations — an early, agency-grade signal of rising dispute volume that precedes named cases.

source_name: Sindikat uprave i pravosuđa Crne Gore (branch union site, AMRRS coverage)
why_relevant: Example of an active Montenegrin branch-union website that reports on AMRRS and dispute practice; serves as a template and pointer for locating the equivalent finance/banking branch union site and its publication habits.

source_name: EBRD — Montenegro country page (where we invest)
why_relevant: Hub page for EBRD's Montenegro portfolio (96 projects, EUR 933m since 2006) linking to project summary documents, country strategy, resident office and news releases that routinely name partner-bank management and organisational change.

source_name: EBRD Project Summary Documents (PSD) — Montenegro bank projects, incl. Montenegrin-language versions
why_relevant: PSDs name the client bank (e.g. Addiko banka AD Podgorica), the sponsor/ownership structure and the business rationale; the Montenegrin-language versions confirm official local naming of institutions, useful for entity resolution and for detecting new banking counterparties (a proxy for organisational change).

source_name: EBRD news releases on Montenegro banking transactions
why_relevant: Signing announcements explicitly name senior executives on both sides (e.g. EBRD VP Banking Matteo Patrone and CKB Management Board Chair Tamas Kamarasi), making them a reliable, dated record of who currently chairs Montenegrin bank management boards.

source_name: EBRD Country Strategy for Montenegro (2026–2031 draft and predecessors)
why_relevant: Country strategies diagnose banking-sector structure, state ownership, governance weaknesses and institutional capacity of the CBCG — an outside baseline against which organisational change can be measured.
